claims.text: Chemical disorder in high-entropy alloys generates severe local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions pin dislocations during dynamic loading.
Distortion-induced dislocation pinning enhances strain-rate sensitivity.
Distortion-induced dislocation pinning enhances work hardening.
Enhanced strain-rate sensitivity and work hardening allow HEAs to combine greater strength and ductility than conventional alloys containing fewer alloying elements.
CrMnFeCoNi can serve as an equiatomic or near-equiatomic, single-phase HEA for the proposed test.
An alloy with fewer alloying elements will have minimal lattice distortions relative to the HEA.
During rapid deformation, lattice distortions act as effective dislocation-pinning sites and delay dislocation motion.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the HEA will have significantly greater dynamic yield strength.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the HEA will have higher strain-rate sensitivity within a particular dynamic strain-rate window.
Relative to the baseline alloy, the HEA will have a higher work-hardening rate within a particular dynamic strain-rate window.
The predicted dynamic response will produce an improved balance of strength and ductility.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply under dynamic deformation at ambient to moderately elevated temperatures when processing and microstructure are controlled.
The mechanism may have limited applicability under quasi-static loading.
The mechanism may have limited applicability in multiphase microstructures.
Twinning or stacking-fault formation may contribute to dynamic behavior under extreme conditions.
